label: Close tab
summary: Closes the chat tab.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button in the engine's chat window.

label: Tab's chat
summary: The chat shown in this chat tab.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla makes it the data context of a part of the engine's chat window, so that part reads from the tab's chat.

label: Chat title
summary: The title of the chat tab, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tab's text in the engine's chat window.

label: Is tab active
summary: Whether the chat tab is the one that is open.
details: Vanilla shows one look of the tab when it is active and another when not.

label: The chat tab itself
summary: The chat tab object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on a chat tab.

label: Chat tabs
summary: The list of tabs of the chat window.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills the tab row of the engine's chat window from it.

label: The chat window itself
summary: The chat window object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses AccessSelf on the generic widget type to pass a window along as an argument, but never on the chat window.

label: Can send message
summary: Whether a message can be sent from the chat window right now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable a control in the engine's chat window; going by the name, the send button. When sending is not possible is not described.

label: Hide chat window
summary: Hides the chat window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button in the engine's chat window.

label: The chat window itself
summary: The chat window object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on the chat window.

label: Send chat message
summary: Sends the message typed in the chat window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it both when Return is pressed in the typing box and when the send button is clicked.

label: Chat window shown
summary: Whether the chat window should be visible right now.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of the engine's chat window. When it says yes is not described.

label: Show chat window
summary: A command that shows the chat window; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it on the chat window.

label: The child generator itself
summary: The child generator object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses AccessSelf only on the generic widget type, never on the child generator.

label: Generations of children
summary: The list of generated groups of child portraits in the portrait editor.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills the 'Child Portrait Previews' part of the portrait editor (a development tool of the engine) from it; each item in turn lists child portraits. Going by the name, each item is one generation.

label: Random children ratio
summary: The share of generated child portraits that are randomized, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the portrait editor's child previews as 'Random children ratio:' with a percentage, and as the value of a slider beside it. That it is the share of randomized children is read from the name.

label: Random ratio changed
summary: Takes in a new random children ratio when its slider in the portrait editor is moved.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the random children ratio slider of the portrait editor's child previews; the slider passes the value itself.

label: Regenerate children
summary: Generates the child portrait previews of the portrait editor again.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button in the portrait editor's child previews.

label: The child generator itself
summary: The child generator object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on the child generator.

label: The child item itself
summary: The child item object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on a child item.

label: Copy DNA to clipboard
summary: A command that probably copies the child's DNA text to the clipboard.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Child DNA
summary: The DNA (the code describing a portrait's looks) of a generated child, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in a multi-line box of the portrait editor's child previews, beside a 'Paste DNA' button.

label: Child DNA for portrait
summary: The DNA of a generated child as text, with portrait options added, for drawing its portrait.
details: Takes a text of options. Vanilla passes `'|environment=environment_standard|camera=camera_head|age=0.25'` and draws the child's portrait from the result with `GetPortraitTextureFromDna`.

label: Is randomized
summary: Whether a generated child in the portrait editor was randomized.
details: Vanilla uses it to show marks on a child portrait in the editor's child previews. What 'randomized' means for the child is not described.

label: Paste DNA
summary: Pastes DNA into a generated child in the portrait editor.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Paste DNA' button of the editor's child previews. Going by the name, the DNA comes from the clipboard.

label: The child item itself
summary: The child item object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on a child item.

label: The claim itself
summary: The claim object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on a claim.

label: Claimed title
summary: The title this claim is on.
details: Vanilla chains it to the title's holder in the character window (Current holder), and uses it as the data context of the claimant faction window. A claim is a character's legal demand on a title.

label: Claim tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this claim, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the hover text of a claim in the character window, and in a localization text with the click hint added below it.

label: Is implicit claim
summary: Whether the claim is an implicit one.
details: The game does not say what implicit means here. Vanilla uses it in the character window to choose which version of a claim entry is shown, together with IsPressed.

label: Is pressed claim
summary: Whether the claim is a pressed one.
details: The game does not say what pressed means here. Vanilla uses it in the character window next to IsImplicit to choose which claim entry is shown.

label: The claim itself
summary: The claim object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on a claim.

label: The claim title item itself
summary: The claim title item object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on a claim title item.

label: Title of the item
summary: The title this entry in the claim list stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it in the claimant faction interaction window: as the data context of a row and to show the title's name. This is a step that moves on to a title, so more title functions can follow it.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this title entry is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed look of the row in the claimant faction window.

label: Title entry click
summary: A command run when this title entry is clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it on the click of a row in the claimant faction window. The game does not say what it does beyond that; the same rows use IsSelected for their pressed look, which hints that it selects the title.

label: The claim title item itself
summary: The claim title item object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: The claimant entry itself
summary: The claimant entry object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on a claimant entry.

label: Can declare claim war
summary: Probably whether the claimant of this entry can declare a war to press the claim.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it with Not and IsCharacter in the artifact details window, to show a part of the row only for character claimants that fail this check.

label: Claimant army makeup
summary: Probably the make-up of the claimant's army.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the artifact details window, which does not say more.

label: Claimant character
summary: The character who is the claimant of this entry.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact details window to show the character's name and as the data context for the character's parts of the row. Vanilla pairs the character parts of the row with IsCharacter.

label: Claimant house
summary: The house that is the claimant of this entry.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact details window to show the house name, the head of the house, and as the data context. Vanilla shows the house parts of the row with IsHouse.

label: Is character claimant
summary: Whether the claimant of this entry is a single character.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact details window to show the parts of a row that are meant for characters.

label: Is house claimant
summary: Whether the claimant of this entry is a house.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact details window to show the parts of a row that are meant for houses.

label: The claimant entry itself
summary: The claimant entry object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: The sort option itself
summary: The claimant sort option object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on a claimant sort option.

label: Sort option name
summary: The name of this way of sorting claimants, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of the sort choices in the title claimants window.

label: The sort option itself
summary: The claimant sort option object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: The claimants window itself
summary: The claimants window object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on the claimants window.

label: Close claimants window
summary: A command that closes the claimants window.
details: Vanilla runs it on the click of the close button in the title claimants window.

label: Claimants
summary: The list of claimants the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list a row list in the title claimants window is built from. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: Parent title window
summary: The title view window this claimants window belongs to.
details: A step that moves on to the title view window, so that window's functions can follow. Vanilla never uses it; this rests on the return type and the name.

label: The claimants window itself
summary: The claimants window object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: The conversion icon itself
summary: The conversion progress icon object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on this icon.

label: Clerical region title
summary: The title of the clerical region the conversion is happening in.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the conversion icon on the map and in the tooltip that says a rite is being spread in a region.

label: Conversion end date
summary: Probably the date the conversion ends, shown in the conversion icon's tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it only in the faiths map mode tooltip that says a rite is being spread in a region; going by its name it is the end date mentioned there.

label: Conversion progress
summary: A number saying how far the conversion has come.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a part of the conversion icon on the map (its name says progress).

label: Conversion rite
summary: The rite that is being spread by this conversion.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the rite's name in the faiths map mode tooltip and the rite's icon on the map icon. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: County title
summary: Probably the county title the conversion icon sits on.
details: Going by its name and its use in the faiths map mode tooltip about a rite being spread; the cut-off text in the input does not show how exactly it is used.

label: The conversion icon itself
summary: The conversion progress icon object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: The elector icon itself
summary: The elector icon object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on this icon.

label: Elector title
summary: The title this elector icon on the map stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the icon in the map icon layer. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: The elector icon itself
summary: The elector icon object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: The cloud save data itself
summary: The cloud save data object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on it.

label: Cloud saves available
summary: Whether saving to the cloud is available.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the cloud save option in the in-game menu.

label: Cloud save tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the cloud save option, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the hover text of the cloud save option in the in-game menu.

label: Cloud save click
summary: A command run when the cloud save option is clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it on the click of the cloud save option in the in-game menu.

label: The cloud save data itself
summary: The cloud save data object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: Should save to cloud
summary: Whether saves go to the cloud.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the cloud save checkbox in the in-game menu.

label: The coat of arms itself
summary: The coat of arms object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on a coat of arms.

label: Coat of arms color
summary: Probably one of the colors of the coat of arms, as a color value; it takes one argument the game does not describe.
details: Going by its name and its color return type. Vanilla never names it on a coat of arms; the lines of other types with the same name only show that GetColor returns a color elsewhere.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: One argument; probably which of the colors is meant.

label: Coat of arms frame
summary: Probably a frame number for the coat of arms; it takes two arguments the game does not describe.
details: Going by its name and its whole-number return type. Vanilla never names it on a coat of arms.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the game does not say.

label: Coat of arms frame with effect
summary: Probably like GetFrame, with an extra argument for an effect; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and its three arguments. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the game does not say.

label: Coat of arms slot
summary: A color-vector slot value for drawing the coat of arms, given two whole numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it in the coat of arms widgets with the same number twice (80, 172 and 230). Going by that, the two numbers look like a width and height in pixels, but the game does not say so. The result is used as the widget's coat of arms slot.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First whole number; vanilla gives it the same value as the second (looks like a width).

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second whole number (looks like a height).

label: Coat of arms slot with effect
summary: Probably like GetSlot, with an extra argument for an effect; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and its three arguments. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the game does not say.

label: Coat of arms texture
summary: The picture of the coat of arms, given two whole numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the coat of arms image of the coat of arms widgets and the designer, with the same number twice (80, 172 and 230). Going by that, the numbers look like a width and height in pixels, but the game does not say so.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First whole number; vanilla gives it the same value as the second (looks like a width).

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second whole number (looks like a height).

label: Coat of arms texture with effect
summary: Probably like GetTexture, with an extra argument for an effect; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and its three arguments. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; the game does not say.

label: The coat of arms itself
summary: The coat of arms object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on a coat of arms.

label: The designer itself
summary: The coat of arms designer object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on the designer.

label: Quartering available
summary: Whether the quartering options are available in the designer.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the quartering options in the coat of arms designer.

label: Can load historical
summary: Whether a historical coat of arms can be loaded in the designer.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the historical coat of arms part of the designer.

label: Can paste design
summary: Whether a coat of arms design on the clipboard can be pasted into the designer.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable and show the paste button, whose tooltip says it pastes the design from the clipboard.

label: Can redo edit
summary: Whether an undone edit can be redone.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the redo button of the designer.

label: Can undo edit
summary: Whether the last edit can be undone.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the undo button of the designer.

label: Palette colors
summary: The list of all colors in the designer's palette.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list the color swatches of the designer are built from. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: Background panel
summary: The designer's panel for the coat of arms background.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the background part of the designer, so background functions can be used inside it.

label: Emblem instances
summary: Probably the emblems placed on the coat of arms; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it; it uses GetEmblemInstancesPanel instead.

label: Emblem instances panel
summary: The designer's panel for the emblems placed on the coat of arms.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the emblem part of the designer, and calls ClearDetailEdit on it from a click.

label: Emblem layout panel
summary: The designer's panel for the layout of the emblems.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the layout part of the designer.

label: Historical coat of arms
summary: The historical coat of arms of the design, as a coat of arms.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the coat of arms picture for the historical version. This is a step that moves on to a coat of arms.

label: Historical coat of arms (long name)
summary: Probably the same as GetHistoricalCoASprite under a longer name: the historical coat of arms.
details: Going by its name and its return type, which match GetHistoricalCoASprite. Vanilla never uses this spelling.

label: Original coat of arms
summary: The original coat of arms of the design, as a coat of arms.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the coat of arms picture for the original version. This is a step that moves on to a coat of arms.

label: Paste preview
summary: The preview of the design that would be pasted from the clipboard.
details: Vanilla chains GetCoA after it to get the coat of arms to draw in the paste preview. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: Preview
summary: The preview of the coat of arms being designed.
details: Vanilla chains GetCoA after it to get the coat of arms drawn in the designer's preview areas. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: Selected culture
summary: The culture currently selected in the designer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of parts of the designer, so culture functions can be used inside. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: Is custom mode
summary: Whether the designer is in custom mode (rather than adjusted mode).
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the designer and to choose between the texts for the custom and the adjusted mode.

label: Is quartering on
summary: Whether quartering is switched on in the designer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the quartering checkbox, and flips it with Not when the box is clicked.

label: Copy design
summary: A command that copies the design to the clipboard.
details: Vanilla runs it from the copy buttons of the designer. The name says the clipboard; the game does not say more.

label: Paste design
summary: A command that pastes a design from the clipboard into the designer.
details: Vanilla runs it from the paste button, whose tooltip says it pastes the coat of arms design from the clipboard.

label: Randomize design
summary: A command that randomizes the design.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the designer. The game does not say exactly what is randomized.

label: Reset to historical
summary: A command that sets the design back to the historical coat of arms.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the designer. Going by the name; vanilla also enables a button with Not of WasDesignResetToHistorical, probably this one.

label: Reset to loaded
summary: A command that sets the design back to the one that was loaded when the designer opened.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the designer. The meaning rests on the name; the game does not describe it.

label: Switch to adjusted mode
summary: A command that switches the designer to adjusted mode.
details: Vanilla runs it from a mode button; the other mode is custom mode (see IsCustomMode).

label: Switch to custom mode
summary: A command that switches the designer to custom mode.
details: Vanilla runs it from mode buttons; the other mode is adjusted mode (see IsCustomMode).

label: Redo edit
summary: A command that redoes the edit that was undone last.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button of the designer; CanRedoEdit enables a button too, probably this one.

label: Save image to disk
summary: A command that saves the coat of arms as an image file, given two whole numbers.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button with 345 twice. Going by the name and that, the numbers look like the image's width and height in pixels, but the game does not say so.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First number; vanilla passes 345 (looks like the width).

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second number; vanilla passes 345 (looks like the height).

label: The designer itself
summary: The coat of arms designer object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on the designer.

label: Set quartering
summary: A command that switches quartering on or off in the designer.
details: Vanilla runs it on the quartering checkbox with the opposite of the current state (Not of IsQuarteringEnabled), so a click toggles it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: yes or no (vanilla passes the opposite of IsQuarteringEnabled)

label: Undo edit
summary: A command that undoes the last edit.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button of the designer; CanUndoEdit enables a button too, probably this one.

label: Was design changed
summary: Whether the design has been changed.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable a button of the designer. The meaning rests on the name and that use.

label: Was reset to historical
summary: Whether the design was set back to the historical coat of arms.
details: Vanilla enables the reset-to-historical button only while this is not the case (it uses Not of it).

label: The background panel itself
summary: The background panel object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on the background panel.

label: All patterns
summary: The list of all background patterns the designer offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list the pattern choices are built from. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: Background color
summary: One of the background's colors as a color value, chosen by its number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tint of the color boxes, with 1, 2 and 3 as the number. So the background has up to three numbered colors.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, written like '(int32)1'; vanilla uses 1, 2 and 3

label: Number of colors
summary: How many colors the background uses.
details: Vanilla shows the color part only when it is greater than 0. The meaning of the count rests on the name and that use.

label: Is color number used
summary: Whether the background uses the color with the given number.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the box of color 1, 2 or 3 only when that color is used.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, written like '(int32)1'; vanilla uses 1, 2 and 3

label: Is palette color selected
summary: Whether a palette color is the one chosen for the given background color number.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a palette swatch as pressed, giving the color number and the swatch's value.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The palette color to compare against.
fields.values: the value of a palette color (vanilla passes CoatOfArmsDesignerPaletteColor.GetValue)

label: Finish color edit
summary: A command run when editing a background color is finished.
details: Vanilla runs it when the editing of a color box ends, with the color number (1, 2 or 3).

label: Select edited color
summary: A command run when a background color was edited in a color box.
details: Vanilla runs it on the color edited event of a color box, with the color number (1, 2 or 3).

label: Select palette color
summary: A command that sets a background color to a color picked from the palette.
details: Vanilla runs it when a palette swatch is clicked, giving the color number and the swatch itself.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which color of the background to set.

label: Select pattern
summary: A command that probably chooses a background pattern; it takes one argument.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: The background panel itself
summary: The background panel object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on this one.

label: Update pattern previews
summary: A command that refreshes the colors of the pattern previews.
details: Vanilla runs it on clicks of color choices, so the pattern previews match the new colors. The meaning rests on the name and that use.

label: The emblem itself
summary: The emblem object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Vanilla uses it as the argument of RemoveEmblemInstance on the emblems panel, on a right click, to say which emblem to remove.

label: Emblem index
summary: The position number of this emblem in the list.

label: Emblem index text

label: Emblem preview
summary: The preview of this emblem.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this emblem is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it for the pressed look of the emblem entry, and shows a part of the entry only while the emblem is not selected.

label: Select emblem
summary: A command that selects this emblem.
details: Vanilla runs it on the default action of an emblem entry.

label: Select emblem for details
summary: A command that selects this emblem to edit its details.

label: Add emblem to selection
summary: A command that adds this emblem to the selection.
details: Vanilla runs it when the entry is clicked with shift held (the onshift event). That it adds to the selection rests on the name Multi and that event.

label: The emblem itself
summary: The emblem object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses Self on many other types to pass the object along as an argument, but never on an emblem.

label: Paged emblem data
summary: Probably the paging data of the emblem list.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the designer. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: The emblem panel itself
summary: The emblem panel object itself, so it can be handed on to another function.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla never names this function on the emblem panel.

label: Add emblem

details: Vanilla runs it on the click of the add button of the emblem list.

label: Clear detail edit
summary: A command that closes the detail edit so no emblem is being edited.
details: Vanilla runs it on clicks in the emblem part of the designer. The meaning rests on the name and that use.

details: Vanilla runs it on every value change of a position control, passing the control itself.

label: Edit emblem y position
summary: A command run while the emblem's vertical position is being changed.
details: Vanilla runs it on every value change of a position control, passing the control itself.

label: Edit emblem rotation
summary: A command run while the emblem's rotation is being changed.
details: Vanilla runs it on every value change of the rotation control, passing the control itself.

label: Edit emblem x scale
summary: A command run while the emblem's horizontal size is being changed.
details: Vanilla runs it on every value change of a scale control, passing the control itself.

label: Edit emblem y scale
summary: A command run while the emblem's vertical size is being changed.
details: Vanilla runs it on every value change of a scale control, passing the control itself.

label: Edit emblem scale together
summary: A command run while the emblem's size is being changed for both directions at once.
details: Vanilla runs it on every value change of the combined scale control, passing the control itself. That it covers both directions rests on the name.

label: Finish emblem x position
summary: A command run when changing the emblem's horizontal position is finished.
details: Vanilla runs it on the change-finished event of the position control, passing the control itself.

label: Finish emblem y position
summary: A command run when changing the emblem's vertical position is finished.
details: Vanilla runs it on the change-finished event of the position control, passing the control itself.

label: Finish emblem rotation
summary: A command run when changing the emblem's rotation is finished.
details: Vanilla runs it on the change-finished event of the rotation control, passing the control itself.

label: Finish emblem x scale
summary: A command run when changing the emblem's horizontal size is finished.
details: Vanilla runs it on the change-finished event of the scale control, passing the control itself.

label: Finish emblem y scale
summary: A command run when changing the emblem's vertical size is finished.
details: Vanilla runs it on the change-finished event of the scale control, passing the control itself.

label: Finish emblem scale together
summary: A command run when changing the emblem's size for both directions at once is finished.
details: Vanilla runs it on the change-finished event of the combined scale control, passing the control itself.

label: All emblems
summary: The list of all emblems placed on the coat of arms.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list the emblem entries are built from (split into pages), to enable a control only when the list has items, and to count the pages in a localization text. Its return type is not registered in the data.

label: Emblem color
summary: One of the emblem's colors as a color value, chosen by its number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tint of the color boxes, with 1, 2 and 3 as the number.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, written like '(int32)1'; vanilla uses 1, 2 and 3
